name: Yitzhak Rabin
role: Prime Minister of Israel (1974-1977, 1992-1995), Defense Minister and IDF chief of staff
summary: Rabin was a Labor Party soldier-statesman who led the IDF to victory in 1967 and later signed the Oslo accords and the peace treaty with Jordan. He held that Israel must stay a militarily strong Jewish state, keep a united Jerusalem and the Jordan Valley, and accept a Palestinian entity short of statehood in exchange for peace. At home his government promised national health insurance, privatization alongside a social-service basket, and closing gaps with Arab citizens. He was assassinated in 1995 by a Jewish opponent of the peace process.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Presenting his government he promised a national health law with public funding so that every citizen has health insurance through public funds.

public-ownership.rationale: His government's programme was to promote the sale of government-owned firms and privatization, in collaboration with the workers.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He said Israel had erred in its treatment of Arab and Druze citizens and promised to close the gaps.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He called it the government's duty to preserve the tie between the State and the Jewish heritage.

direct-votes.rationale: He promised that any significant Golan withdrawal would go to a national referendum, asking what is more democratic than that.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: At his last public appearance he said violence erodes the basis of Israeli democracy and must be condemned and isolated; decisions are made in elections; after the Hebron massacre he called the shooter's aim political and vowed to resist the blackmail of the trigger.

military-superiority.rationale: As ambassador to the US he procured advanced American weapons for Israel, and as Defense Minister (1984-90, 1992-95) he led its military.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He aspired to a Jewish state at least 80% of whose citizens are Jews, while promising non-Jewish citizens full civil rights.

conscription.rationale: He said citizens are called to enlist in the army to defend lives, and as Defense Minister ran a conscript IDF.

universal-morality.rationale: He described the sanctity of life as one universal message that can embrace the whole world and be common to different regimes and cultures.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He said the land was restored after two thousand years to its lawful owners, the Jewish people, and that the government chose to be a Jewish state.

national-self-determination.rationale: He called the Palestinians a separate national entity yet said they would have an entity less than a state, so he rejected a state for them.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: His government decided to have the Attorney General explore outlawing the Kach and Kahane Hai organizations after the Hebron massacre.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He named the homeless, overcrowded families and development towns as first in the new order of priorities, with preference for fighting unemployment.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: His government imposed administrative detentions and disarmed radical settlers after the Hebron massacre.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He signed agreements withdrawing the IDF from Gaza, Jericho and West Bank cities and agreed border corrections with Jordan, giving up territory for peace; Britannica reports he froze new settlements and signed the Israel-PLO accords and Jordan treaty.

holocaust-denial.rationale: He spoke of the millions who perished in the Holocaust and of children marched to slaughter and women at the gates of the crematoria.

social-market-economy.rationale: He paired privatization and a freer economy with a legally guaranteed basket of public social services and pensions.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He said Israel is prepared for war if forced on it and that sometimes the only way to defend citizens is to fight.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: He called ingathering and immigration essential ('without all this, we will not have a return to Zion') and pledged to raise immigration.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: He called Jerusalem the focus of Jewish longing and spoke of the return to Zion and the land of the prophets.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: He called attacks on civilians murderous terrorism and cited the IDF code requiring soldiers to avoid harming innocents, including on the enemy side.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He treated Palestinian armed attacks on Israelis and soldiers in the territories as murderous terrorism to be fought, and urged an end to violence.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He promised a basket of social services provided by law to all citizens covering education, health, welfare and housing.

notes: Positions come from Rabin's major speeches 1992-1995 (government programme, Nobel lecture, Knesset statements, last rally). Themes searched: economy, society, government, world, liberty, means. Also read: Council of Europe address (28 Jan 1994), Knesset statement on the Declaration of Principles and the Jerusalem address; they state general democratic and religious-tolerance values but settle no specific statement, so they are not cited. The record has no further domestic, religion-and-state, class or decentralisation positions (memoirs unavailable; Knesset roll calls start 2003), so the uncertainty rule is expected to fail on those lines. Statements whose topic he never addressed are null.
